MA Quddus Sheikh, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Md Mozzammel Hoque, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Muslemuddin, Assistant Attorney-General -----For the Respondents.
parties:
Hosne Ara Begum ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Chairman, 1st Court of Settlement ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Mir Hashmat Ali J: This Rule nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned judgment vide Annexure 'D' should not be declared to have been made without jurisdiction and is of no legal effect and why the holding No. L/1, Block-E, Mohammadpur, Dhaka should not be released from the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings published on 23-9-1986. 

2. The petitioner filed Settlement Case No. 130 of 1997 before the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

3. The petitioner challenged the judgment and order dated 22-2-2001 passed by the Chairman, Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka in Settlement Case No. 130 of 1997 (Annexure 'D' to the writ petition). 

4. The short facts of the petitioner's case is that, the then Government of East Pakistan executed and registered the schedule property in favour of Md Nayeem for a period of 99 years. While the said allotec was in possession and enjoying the property peacefully, the Administrative Office of Mohammadpur issued Memo No. 2374(1) AO dated 8-10-1963 a PRF certificate (Annexure-'R-1'). Thereafter, the original lessee Md Nayeem transferred the property to Mrs Asma Khatoon, wife of Mr Shahabuddin Ahmed vide sale deed No. 13999 registered on 12-10-1963 (Annexure-'R-2'). After purchase Asma Khatoon made lot of improvements of the said property. Thereafter, the said Asma Khatoon obtained permission for construction of a house from the office of the Authorised Officer, Dhaka Improvement Trust on 19-3-1964 vide Memo No. 1118 TP dated 19-3-1964 (Annexure-'R-3'). Thereafter, Section Officer of the Deputy Commissioner's office under Ministry of Works vide his Memo No. 1010/CHB, dated 10-8-1964 issued a letter informing Mrs Asma Khatoon regarding mutation certificate (Annexure-'R-4'). Thereafter, said Mrs Asma Khatoon mortgaged the case property to the House Building Finance Corporation, Dhaka under mortgage deed No. 5843 dated 22-6-1965 against loan case No. D1728 and after obtaining loan, said Mrs Asma Khatoon constructed a three-storied building on the case property (Annexure-'R-5'). While the said Mrs Asma Khatoon was enjoying the property peacefully, she desired to sell out the property and the petitioner offered to purchase the same at a consideration of Taka 50,000 and accordingly, Mrs Asma Khatoon accepted the money and entered into an agreement for sale with the petitioner on 13-12-1970 and on the date of agreement, the petitioner was partly put into possession of the case property as part performance of the contract. Subsequently, the petitioner paid five thousand Taka to the said Asma Khatoon and endorsed the same in the back side of the agreement for sale (Annexure-'J'). Subsequently, the said Asma Khatoon was requested to execute a sale deed but she did not. Consequently, the petitioner filed Suit No. 1084 of 1981 for specific performance of contract before the 4th Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. Ultimately, the said suit was decreed on 25-5-1983. The aforesaid decree was put into execution in Title Execution Case No. 31 of 1983 and got kabala deed executed and registered on 10-8-1983 and the petitioner was put into possession officially in execution case on 2-1-1984 and the petitioner till date enjoying the same without any hindrance from any quarter (Annexure-F, Fl, F2, F3 and F4). The petitioner applied before the Deputy Commissioner, Housing and Settlement for mutation of the case property in her name on 8-3-1984 and the Assistant Commissioner issued letter vide Memo No. 7706/1(2)ক, মে dated 4-11-1985 asking the writ petitioner to appear before him with all documents in support of her claim (Annexure-C and C1 ). While the petitioner was enjoying the property peacefully; since the name of the petitioner was not yet mutated; the petitioner used to make payment in the name of his earlier owner Asma Khatun and paid all Electric Bills, Water Bills, Gas Bills, etc. to the concerned authority of the Government accordingly (Annexure-G, G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6 and 07). While the petitioner was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the property, the respondent-government, without serving any notice, most illegally enlisted the property of the petitioner in the "ka" list of the abandoned buildings which was published on 23-9-1986 in serial No. 149 9762(24). Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application under section 7(1) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 challenging the inclusion of the property in the list of abandoned property before the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka. Subsequently, the said case has been marked and numbered as Case No. 130 of 1997. 

5. After hearing of the parties, the Court of Settlement in slipshod manner disposed of the case without proper consideration of the documentary evidence on record (Annexure-'D'). The petitioner during the trial filed an application for calling for the record of the loan Case No. 1728 dated 22-6-1965 from the House Building Finance Corporation as the property was mortgaged to the House Building Finance Corporation. But the said application was neither accepted nor rejected. In the meantime, the House Building Finance Corporation filed Miscellaneous Case No. 377 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka under Article 27(1) of the House Building Finance Corporation Act, 1952 (PO 7 of 1973). In the said miscellaneous case, the petitioner was added as opposite party No. 2. After contested hearing the District Judge, Dhaka was pleased to pass the judgment on 29-6-2000 in favour of respondent No. 3, House Building Finance Corporation and the petitioner was directed to pay the entire loan amount within three months (Annexure-'N'). The petitioner paid the entire decretal amount (loan amount) to the respondent No. 3, House Building Finance Corporation within time (Annexure-'O' series). Subsequently, House Building Finance Corporation issued clearance certificate in respect of full payment of the decretal amount (Annexure-'S').

6. The petitioner finding no other alternative filed instant writ petition and obtained Rule. 

7. Mr MA Quddus Sheikh, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the petitioner purchased the property under an agreement which was prior to 25th March, 1971 and that such agreement was binding upon the Government as well as upon the original owner. In such situation the same allotment may be cancelled, amended or terminated by the Government, if it so chooses to do so and that the possessors of the abandoned property could be asked to surrender the possession under the provision of President's Order No. 16 of 1972 (Clause-1 of Article 10 of the PO 16 of 1972). In the instant case there was no such termination of the agreement so as to entitle the Government to take over possession and, as such, the possession of the petitioner on the basis of the agreement for sale cannot be termed to be an unauthorised one. The Government never choose to terminate the agreement but instead left it to be held a valid document and made itself binding on it and in such circumstances the possession is protected under section 53(A) of the Transfer of Property Act entitling the petitioner to exercise his right to maintain possession. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Bangladesh vs Kazi Ashrafuddin Ahmed reported in 55 DLR (AD) 16. He further submits that the government got the abandoned property from the possession of the petitioner as required under section 7 of the PO 16 of 1972. In support of his contention, he has pointed out the Memo No. A M-19/60/7706/1(2)/ka, say, dated 4-12-1985 (Annexure-C1)" requesting the petitioner to appear before the Assistant Commissioner, Settlement with all the valid documents in regard to the property and that in the said letter the administrative officer was asked to inquire into the matter as to who is in possession and whether he has paid all the dues of the government, which shows that at least till 4-12-1985 the property was not declared as an abandoned property and, as such, the question of abandonment under PO 16 of 1972 is misconceived and Court of Settlement failed to consider such aspect of the case. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Mahmuda Begum vs 1st Court of Settlement reported in 13 BLC 247. He further submits that before enlistment of the property in the list of abandoned property no notice was served upon the petitioner as required under PO 16 of 1972 and under Ordinance 54 of 1985. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Abdur Rashid Mollah vs Bangladesh reported in 58 DLR (AD) 20, the case of Bangladesh vs Amela Khatoon reported in 53 DLR (AD) 55 and the case of Bangladesh vs Helaluddin Ahmed reported in 4 MLR (AD) 140. He further submits that the Court of Settlement on misconception of law failed to consider that the original owner Mohammad Nayeem transferred the property to Asma Khatun and Asma Khatun transferred the same to the petitioner under an agreement dated 13-12-70, which was before Liberation and before the promulgation of President's Order 16 of 1972 and all such transfers cannot be disturbed by the government as per Article 10(1) of PO 16 of 1972 because those transfer were made much earlier than 25th March, 1971. He further submits that the Court of Settlement disposed of the case on the basis of the reported case 47 DLR (AD) 71 but in the facts and circumstances of the present case 47 DLR (AD) 71 is not applicable. In the instant case, the ex parte decree was obtained for enforcement of an agreement entered into before promulgation of PO 16 of 1972 and also before 25th March, 1971 and such agreement was not after the promulgation of PO 16 of 1972. He further submits that any ex parte decree obtained in respect of the agreement after 25th March, 1971 cannot be enforceable according to 47 DLR (AD) 71. But in the instant case admittedly, the agreement was executed long before PO 16 of 1972 and 25th March, 1971. He further submits that admittedly the property was mortgaged to the House Building Finance Corporation in Loan Case No. D-1728 before liberation of Bangladesh and before PO 16 of 1972 came into operation and the House Building Finance Corporation (PO 7 of 1973) filed Miscellaneous Case No. 377 of 1999 before the District Judge, Dhaka and the learned District Judge after hearing both the parties decreed the suit against the opposite parties including the petitioner and according to the said decree, the petitioner paid entire dues of the decretal amount to the House Buildings Finance Corporation. 

8. He further submits that the property was mortgaged to the House Building Finance Corporation which was incorporated under Act 18 of 1952. Subsequently, the said Act has been incorporated in Bangladesh in PO 7 of 1973 and, as such, practically, property mortgaged to the House Building Finance Corporation means to the Government and such property which was mortgaged to Government organisation cannot be declared as abandoned property. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Ariff A Shekha vs Bangladesh reported in 47 DLR 289 the case of Gannysons Ltd vs Sonali Bank reported in 37 DLR (AD) 42 and the case of Md Zaher vs Bangladesh reported in 42 DLR 430. 

9. He further submits that the petitioner filed series of documents before the Court of Settlement including the document of allotment and lease of the property from the Government since from 1963. But the Court of Settlement without considering those documents dismissed the case of the petitioner in a slipshod manner and, as such, the impugned judgment and order dated 22-2-2001 passed by the Court of Settlement in Case No. 130 of 1997 should be declared to have been made and passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

10. Mr Md Mozzammel Hoque, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the respondents, submits that the petitioner failed to prove the case before the Court of Settlement and the burden of proof lies upon him and, as such, burden cannot be shifted to others. In support of his contention, he cited the case of Kuinbhan Lakshmanna vs Tangirala Venkateswarla reported in 2 DLR 83. 

11. We have heard the learned Advocates of both the parties at length and perused the writ petition, supplementary affidavits on behalf of the petitioner, application for addition of party and affidavit-in-opposition and the annexure thereof 

12. It appears that in the writ petition, several supplementary affidavits of various days and application for addition of party, the petitioner annexed various documents of the case property. We have checked up the record of the case, it appears that the husband of the petitioner was examined as PW 1 and he has placed all the documents of the case property including the mortgage of the property to the House Building Finance Corporation. But the Court of Settlement rejected all those documents on the ground that the witness PW 1 could not say the whereabouts of the witnesses of the agreement at present. But the Court of Settlement failed to consider that deed of agreement was executed on 13-12-1970 long before the liberation of Bangladesh and the evidence was taken on 10-10-2000 after about 30 years and that such agreement was also tested and believed by the Civil Court and the Court of Settlement failed to appreciate that none could say the whereabouts of the persons who are witnesses and scribe of the document after long 30 years, that too pre-liberation, but the case of the petitioner was dismissed only on that ground without considering the other documents. It further appears that the Court of Settlement rejected plea of ex parte decree of the petitioner on the ground of a reported case 47 DLR (AD) 71 on the ground that the decree was obtained on the basis of an agreement after the promulgation of President's Order 16 of 1972 but fact remains that the agreement was executed long before PO 16 of 1972 came into operation and before 25th March, 1971, before liberation of Bangladesh and, as such, the case of specific performance of contract before the liberation cannot be construed and considered a bar under PO 16 of 1972. It has already been held in the case of Bangladesh vs Kazi Ashrafuddin Ahmed reported in 55 DLR (AD) 16 and the case of Mahmuda Begum vs First Court of Settlement reported in 13 Inc 247, which runs thus: 

"From the provision of Article 10, it seems to be clear that any allotment or lease of or any agreement relating to an abandoned property is binding upon the government as custodian subject to its right as conferred under the said provisions. It appears that any allotment, lease or agreement granted or entered into before the 25th March, 1971 is binding upon the Government in the same way as upon the original owner having entered into the shoes of the lawful owner but the allotment agreement or lease granted or entered into after 25th March, 1971 may be cancelled, terminated or amended by the Government, if it chooses to do so, and if a person is in possession of an abandoned property by virtue of such allotment, lease or agreement can be asked to surrender possession of such property only if the Government cancels or terminates such an allotment, lease or agreement under clause (2) of the Article and, as is provided in clause (3) the Government may eject such a person only when he fails to surrender possession under clause (2) of the Article. 

In the instant Rule, agreement for sale dated 27-12-1970 i.e. prior to 25th March, 1971, and considering from this standpoint it appears that the said agreement dated 27-12-1970 does not come within the purview of Article 10 of the PO of 1972 unconditionally but subject to terms and conditions of the agreement for sale. The provisions of said Order do not confer any power upon the Government, which appears from Article 10, to ignore an agreement entered into after 25th March, 1971 and eject the occupant lawfully in possession of the abandoned property". 

13. In the instant case, we find from Annexure-'C-1' that Assistant Commissioner, Settlement vide Memo No. A M-19/60/7706/1(2)/ka, se dated 4-12-1985 directed the Administrative Officer of Mohammadpur Housing Estate, Dhaka to enquire as to whether any person is living in the house or whether they have paid the dues of the government and in the said letter the petitioner was asked to submit the original lease deed, original agreement, original purchase deed and original judgment of the Civil Court before the Assistant Commissioner, which shows that at least up to 4-12-1985 the property was not declared as an abandoned property and that at least the petitioner was in possession up to 4-12-1985. 

Admittedly, the case property was mortgaged to the House Building Finance Corporation in House Building Finance Corporation Loan Case No. D-1728 dated 22-6-1965 and that the House Building Finance Corporation filed Miscellaneous Case No. 377 of 1999 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka for realisation of loan against petitioner and others and, as such, we find at least up to decree dated 29-6-2000 the property was under mortgage to House Building Finance Corporation. But such aspect of the case has not been considered by the Court of Settlement though the petitioner agitated the matter before the Court of Settlement. 

14. It has been held in the case of Ariff A Shekha vs Bangladesh reported in 47 DLR 289, that: 

"As the company and its shares have been vested under PO 27 of 1972 on the ground that it was vested in the Government as an abandoned property, under PO 16 of 1972 if it is found that the company and shares thereof does not carry abandoned character then the shares of the petitioners who were found to have been away from the country and have been residing as its national in any country which was not at war with Bangladesh could not be treated as abandoned shares." 

In the instant case, admittedly the property was mortgaged to House Building Finance Corporation, which is an organisation under the Government of Bangladesh according to PO 7 of 1973. 

15. Let us see, what is the meaning of the mortgage. According to Judicial Dictionary of KJ Aiyar, mortgage is defined as under, "a mortgage' is the transfer of an interest in specific immovable property for securing the payment of money, or a present or future debt It may be—
(a) simple, that is, without possession or 
(b) usufructuary, that is, with possession. 

16. In a simple mortgage, both the ownership and possession remain vested in the owner. The form of security only entitles the creditor, in default of repayment of his debt, to realise it by eventual sale of the mortgaged property. But, in a usufructuary mortgage, the owner parts with possession of the mortgaged property. It has been held in the case of Zaher vs Bangladesh reported in 42 DLR 430 that the section 2(i)(ii)(b) clearly provides that any property which was taken over by the Government under any other law before President's Order No. 16 of 1972 came into force could not be located as an abandoned property. Admittedly, the suit property was requisitioned on 14-2-1972 as per order of requisition and was taken over possession as such on 16-2-1972 by the Government before President's Order No. 16 of 1972 came into force. That being the position the suit property could not be treated as abandoned property. 

17. In the instant case, the House Building Finance Corporation filed Miscellaneous Case No. 377 of 1999 for sale of the property for recovery of debts and obtained decree for the amount and the petitioner on payment of decretal amount released the property from House Building Finance Corporation and, as such, it appears that the property was under House Building Finance Corporation (government organisation), that being the position the property in question cannot be treated as abandoned property but the Court of Settlement failed to consider such aspect of the case in its proper perspective. 

18. It further appears that admittedly up to 4-12-1985 the property was not declared as an abandoned property and, as such, subsequent enlistment of the property is to be made after proper service of notice as contemplated under Article 7(3) of PO 16 of 1972 and section 5(1)(a) of Ordinance No. 54 of 1995. But in the instant case, the respondents Government failed to show any such notice served upon the petitioner or upon her predecessor. Rather, we find from Memo No. A M-19/60/7706/1(2)/ ka, se dated 4-12-1985 that the petitioner was asked to produce the relevant original documents of the property before Assistant Commissioner, Settlement. It appears that the petitioner obtained ex parte decree from the civil Court and by dint of the said decree execution case was filed and she obtained registered deed and also obtained legal possession through Court. Though we find that the petitioner is in possession since from date of agreement 1970. No doubt the petitioner is to prove her case before the Court of Settlement as series of decisions have been made that the person who claims is to prove the case. The husband of the petitioner, on evidence, produced all the documents in accordance with law before the Court of Settlement but Court of Settlement without considering all the documents held an erroneous view that the witness was not able to say whereabouts of the scribe and the witnesses of the agreement. But we find that the evidence was taken long after 30 years and during the period none could say whereabouts of the persons who were present 30 years ago and that the said agreement has been tested before the Civil Court earlier and, as such, finding made by the tribunal is not a proper finding of facts and a perverse proposition and, as such, we find that the Court of Settlement did not consider the case of the petitioner to its proper perspective and, as such, we feel that justice will be met if we send the case on remand to the Court of Settlement for proper consideration and disposal of the case. 

19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. 

20. The impugned judgment and order dated 22-2-2001 passed by the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka in Settlement Case No. 130 of 1997 (ka-149, Block-E, Mohammadpur, Dhaka) in respect of House No. L/1, Block-E, Mohammadpur, Dhaka is hereby set aside. 

21. The Settlement Case No. 130 of 1997 (ka-149, Block-E, Mohammadpur, Dhaka) in respect of House No. L/1, Block-E, Mohammadpur, Dhaka is remanded back to the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka for proper disposal of the case in accordance with law. In the meantime, parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession and position of the case property till disposal of the Settlement Case No. 130 of 1997 of the Court of Settlement, 1st Court, Dhaka. 

The petitioner is permitted to take back the original documents by substituting photostat of the same within 1(one) month and file the same before the Court of Settlement. 

End.
